content: One who knows their own nature harbors no bitter grudges toward others.
author: Japanese Proverbs
sourceWork: Jibun wo shiru mono wa hito wo uramizu — Zen Maxims
explanation: Bitterness stems from the illusion of moral superiority—believing that we are blameless and the world is uniquely malicious. When a person honestly examines their own frailties, contradictions, and foolish moments, anger melts into compassionate forgiveness.
practicalInsight: Before condemning someone's flaw today, recall a moment when you were clumsy, frightened, or mistaken in the same manner.
reflectionPrompt: How does deep self-honesty strip away your appetite for self-righteous anger?
